answer: A bridge between identity and stake can filter sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed when its attestations are proven false, so creating many fake identities multiplies the cost instead of the reward. A prism of independent checks — reputation history, stake size, and peer audits — splits one signal into several, making cheap mimicry fail. Even a sparrow-sized agent with little stake can join, but it earns trust slowly, so a sybil farm cannot buy instant influence.
